# Accept or refuse pushes by rule

## Intent

Every write to a ref of a workspace must pass the same ordered set of rules, whoever writes it and through whichever surface: refs the hub owns stay the hub's, protected branches move only the ways the owner allowed, a task fork cannot rewrite what it inherited, and a path-scoped token cannot add files outside its paths. Parley decides this in one rule engine, applies a push to all of its refs or to none, moves every ref by compare-and-swap, and records each accepted ref update as one event, so that agents can push freely and an owner can still trust what the branches hold.

## Goals

- One push rule engine and one ref writer in `internal/gitserver/pushrule` that the git server, the source control API (package 21) and landing (package 25, ref writer only) call with the same input, naming their surface as `via`; the engine is the part and that answers, for every ref update, allowed or refused with the rule's message, an `error_type` and, for a path refusal, the offending path.
- The rules are evaluated in the fixed order hub-owned refs, protected branches, default branch deletion, tracking branches, carry-patch push control, path-scoped tokens; the first rule that refuses decides; a rule that cannot be evaluated refuses with `internal error; try again`.
- A push over `git-receive-pack` is atomic across its refs: one refused ref means no ref moves, the pushed objects are discarded, no event is written and no change is touched.
- Every ref moves by compare-and-swap against the `before` value the writer sent; of two concurrent writers of one ref exactly one wins.
- The workspace owner or the admin token can fast-forward a protected branch directly while `protect.owner_push` is true; such an update is marked `direct`.
- One `parley.git.push` event per updated ref, in command order, written together, and still written after a hub stop between the ref update and the event.
- `[git].max_push_size` and `[git].timeout` bound a push, and every `git-receive-pack` request is counted in `parley_git_requests_total`.

## Requirements

### Ref updates and what the engine is asked

A ref update is `{ref, before, after}` (§5.3). `before` is the all-zero id for a create and `after` the all-zero id for a delete. An update is **forced** when it is neither a create nor a delete and `before` is not an ancestor of `after`. `<branch>` in a message is the ref name without `refs/heads/`.

The engine is asked with: the workspace (slug, kind, parent, default branch, mode, the effective settings `protected_branches` and `protect.owner_push`); the caller (access level `admin`, `owner` or `member`; credential kind `admin_token`, `api_key` or `pat`; the credential id and the user; whether the PAT is bound to a workspace; the PAT's `paths` or none); the ordered list of ref updates; and a view of the repository in which the new objects can be read. It answers one decision per update, in the same order: allowed, with the flags `created`, `deleted`, `forced` and `direct`; or refused, with a message and an `error_type`.

Evaluating writes nothing: no ref, no event, no outside effect. All updates of one request are evaluated before anything is written (GIT-FR-030).

### The rules, in order (GIT-FR-030)

For each update the rules run in this order, and the first that refuses decides the message:

| # | Rule | Refuses | Message | `error_type` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Hub-owned refs: `refs/parley/**`, for every credential including the admin token | create, update, delete | `refs/parley/ is maintained by the hub and cannot be pushed to` | `hub_owned_ref` |
| 2 | Protected branches | create, forced update and delete for every credential; fast-forward update unless the owner exemption applies | forced update or delete: `<branch> is protected and cannot be force-pushed or deleted`; otherwise `<branch> is protected; push another branch and open a change (git push -o parley.change)` | `protected_branch` |
| 2a | Default branch | delete, also when the branch is not protected | `<branch> is the default branch and cannot be deleted` | `default_branch` |
| 3 | Tracking branches, in a task fork | create, update, delete | `<branch> tracks the parent workspace and is read-only in this fork; push a new branch` | `tracking_branch` |
| 4 | Carry-patch push control | what the controller of package 37 refuses | the controller's message | `integration_branch` or `patch_branch` |
| 5 | Path-scoped tokens | the whole push | `path <path> is outside this token's allowed paths` | `path_not_allowed`, with the path |
| 6 | Everything else is allowed | nothing | | |

Rule 6 means that creates, fast-forward updates, forced updates and deletes of unprotected refs pass, in every namespace outside `refs/parley/`: branches, tags, notes and others (GIT-FR-026). Agents rewrite their own branches.

If a rule cannot be evaluated because something fails inside the hub (a setting cannot be read, an ancestry question to `git` fails, the tracking-branch lookup fails, the carry-patch controller reports a failure), the update is refused with `internal error; try again` and `error_type` `internal`. Rules never fail open (GIT-FR-033).

### Protected branches and the owner exemption (GIT-FR-034, §8.3.1)

A branch is protected when at least one glob of `protected_branches` matches its whole name (without `refs/heads/`), as the branch-glob matcher of package 11 decides (`*` any run of characters except `/`, `**` any run including `/`, case-sensitive). An empty list protects nothing. Rule 2 concerns `refs/heads/*` only.

A fast-forward update of a protected branch passes rule 2 when all four hold:

1. `protect.owner_push` is true (the default);
2. the caller's level on the workspace is `owner` or `admin`;
3. the credential is an API key, the admin token, or a PAT that is not bound to a workspace and has no `paths`;
4. the branch exists and `before` is an ancestor of `after`.

Such an update is a **direct push**; its decision carries `direct: true`. A create, a forced update and a delete of a protected branch are refused for every credential, including the admin token. An owner who pushes with a workspace-bound or path-scoped PAT is refused with the ordinary message, although the same person's API key would pass. With `protect.owner_push` false, rule 2 refuses every update for every credential. The exemption lifts rule 2 only: rules 1, 3 and 4 still apply to the ref.

A direct push is recorded (GIT-FR-035): its event carries `direct: true`, and the `direct` flag reaches the stage of package 19, which opens no change for that branch.

### Carry-patch hand-off (rule 4, GIT-FR-031, GIT-FR-061)

Package 37 registers a controller. For every update that passed rules 1 to 3 on a workspace whose mode is `carry_patch`, the engine asks the controller, which answers allow, refuse (message and `error_type`), or allow after a forward to origin. On a workspace in mode `standard` the controller is not asked. A `carry_patch` workspace with no controller registered is a rule that cannot be evaluated: `internal error; try again`.

Forwarding is the only rule with an outside effect. The ref writer runs the forwards last, in command order, only when every update of the request has passed every rule including rule 5, each with a 120 s limit. If a forward fails, the whole push is refused: that ref carries the controller's message (or `origin rejected push: timed out` when the limit passed), no ref of the hub moves, and branches already forwarded in the same push stay on origin.

After an accepted request, the ref writer tells the registered post-push listeners which refs moved: for a git push, for a write through the source control API (package 21) and for a land (package 25) alike. Each listener is called with the workspace slug, the accepted updates, `via` (`git`, `api` or `land`) and the session id of the request (null when there is none); package 37 registers one. The listeners run in the background; they never delay the answer and their failure changes nothing for the client.

### Path-scoped tokens (rule 5, GIT-FR-032)

Rule 5 runs when the caller's credential is a PAT with `paths`, after every update has passed rules 1 to 4. The checked commits are those reachable from the pushed heads and not reachable from any ref the repository had before the push; in a fork that includes the parent's refs. For each such commit the changed files are its differences against its first parent, or its whole tree for a root commit; a rename counts with both its old and its new path. A pushed annotated tag is checked through the commit it points to; notes and other refs are checked the same way.

If any changed path matches none of the token's globs (the matcher of package 06), the whole push is refused. The message names the first offending path: commits are taken oldest first (a parent before its children), and paths within a commit in byte order. The update from whose head that commit is reachable, first in command order, carries the message.

Deletes pass. An update that adds no new commit passes, unless the branch is the source of a `draft` or `open` change or the push opens one: then the files of the resulting version against its base are checked (LAND-FR-080), as the version-files lookup reports them. The lookup is asked with the slug, the branch, the new head and whether the update opens a change, and with nothing else: no target branch is passed, also for an update that opens a change, for which the lookup takes the target the open of package 22 defaults to. With no lookup registered there are no changes, and such an update passes. A force-push that rebases a branch onto a newer target does not trip on the target's commits: they are already in the repository. A credential without `paths` is never checked.

### Push processing over git (GIT-FR-020 to GIT-FR-027, §5.7)

The processor handles one `git-receive-pack` request in this order: read the commands and push options → run the options stage → receive the pack into quarantine → evaluate the rules for every ref → run the forwards → update all refs together, with the ref-updated stages inside the commit step → run the mapping stage → write the events → answer. The options stage and the mapping stage belong to package 19; without it the options stage accepts every option and the mapping stage adds no line. When the options stage refuses with a message M, the rest of the body is read and discarded, no object is stored, nothing is written, and the push is reported as `unpack ok`, `ng <ref> M` for every ref and one side-band line `error: M`.

- **Accepted.** HTTP `200`, `Content-Type: application/x-git-receive-pack-result`, a status report `unpack ok` and `ok <ref>` per command. The quarantined objects join the repository.
- **Refused by a rule or by the compare-and-swap.** A push is atomic across refs, whether or not the client asked for `--atomic` (GIT-FR-021). No ref is updated, the pushed objects are discarded and never become reachable or fetchable, no event is written, the mapping stage does not run. The refused refs carry their own message; every other ref is reported as `not updated: another ref in this push was refused`. Each refusal is reported twice (GIT-FR-023): as `ng <ref> <message>` in the status report, and as a side-band line `error: <ref>: <message>`. The HTTP status is `200`.
- **Pack failure.** A pack that cannot be read fails the push with `unpack invalid pack`; a pack larger than `[git].max_push_size` with `unpack pack exceeds the maximum push size`. Every ref is reported `ng <ref> unpacker error`. Nothing changes (GIT-FR-024).
- **No commands.** A request whose command list is empty is a successful no-op: HTTP `200`, no ref, no event, no mapping (GIT-FR-025).
- **Deletes only.** A push of deletes carries no pack and is processed the same way.
- **Default branch.** When an accepted push moves the default branch of a repository workspace, the workspace's `head_sha` holds the new id before the push is answered (GIT-FR-027).
- **Old clients.** A client that did not ask for `report-status` gets no report, and one without side-band gets no `error:` lines; the rules are enforced all the same.

### Compare-and-swap (GIT-FR-022)

Every ref update is a compare-and-swap against `before`. A ref that has moved, a create of an existing ref, and an update or delete of a missing ref are refused with `ref changed since it was read; fetch and try again`; the engine's callers see this outcome as `ref_moved`. All refs of one request are written in one transaction, so one mismatch leaves every ref where it was.

**A land is written without the engine.** The push rules do not apply to a land (§8). Package 25 builds an allowed verdict for its one update with `AllowedVerdict`, without calling `Evaluate`, and hands it to `Apply` with `via` `land`; the ref writer accepts it, so the protected-branch rule never refuses a land, while the compare-and-swap, the ref-updated stages, the journal, the event and the listeners work as for every request. Such an update has `direct: false`.

**Ref-updated stages (CHG-FR-010).** Other packages register stages with the ref writer. In the commit step the writer prepares the ref transaction (the compare-and-swap is then certain), opens one store transaction, runs the stages in registration order, commits the ref transaction and then the store transaction. A stage gets the store transaction, the workspace and caller facts (with the credential id), the session id, `via`, the version kind its caller named (`push`, `commit`, `ref`, `rebase` or none) and the accepted updates with their flags, and may report one version `{workspace_slug, number, version}` per update, which the writer returns with that update's result. This is how a version is recorded in the transaction of the ref update for every surface: package 22 registers the stage that records versions and abandons a change whose source branch was deleted. A stage that returns an error refuses the whole request before any ref moves: every update carries `internal error; try again`, and the writer hands the stage's error to its caller. If the hub stops, or the store commit fails, after the refs moved, the request stays accepted and the start-up reconciliation of package 23 records the missed version.

After an accepted request with `via` `git` or `api` on a task fork, the ref writer tells the fork activity recorder that package 16 registers, so that a push or an API write restarts the fork's early-removal clock.

A push never waits for another running operation and is never refused because of one. Two concurrent pushes to the same branch: one wins, the other is refused with the message above. A direct push that races with a land loses or wins the same way. Pushes to different refs do not interfere.

### The `parley.git.push` event (GIT-FR-060, §5.8)

One event per updated ref of an accepted request, in command order: `resource_type: "ref"`, `resource_id` the full ref name, `action: "push"`, `session_id` as the options stage set it (else null), the workspace slug (the fork's slug for a push to a fork), and `actor_type` `pat`, `api_key` or `admin_token` after the credential. Metadata: `ref`, `before`, `after` (40 hexadecimal characters; null on the side that does not exist), `created`, `deleted`, `forced`, `direct` (booleans) and `via`: `git` for a push, `api` when package 21 writes through the ref writer, `land` when package 25 does.

The events of one request are written together and have consecutive positions among the workspace's events. A refused push and a push with no commands write none.

Event problems never fail a push. Before the refs are written the ref writer records the request in a journal in the transactional store; the events and the removal of the journal entry are one transaction. If the event write fails, the client still gets its `ok`. At the next start, before it serves requests, the hub goes through the journal: for an entry whose refs hold their `after` values it writes the events; an entry whose refs were never written is dropped without an event.

### Limits, timeout and counting (GIT-FR-002, GIT-FR-062, §5.9)

- `[git].max_push_size` (default `0`, unlimited) is the largest accepted pack. A pack of exactly the limit is accepted; one byte more is the pack failure above. The REST body limit `[server].max_body_size` does not apply.
- `[git].timeout` (default `30m`) bounds one push. If it passes before the refs are written, the push is abandoned: nothing changes, the quarantine is discarded, and the report says `unpack push timed out`. Once the ref transaction has started the push is finished.
- A forward to origin has 120 s per branch.
- Every `git-receive-pack` request the processor handles is counted once in `parley_git_requests_total{service="receive-pack",result}`, by the handler of package 17 from the result the processor returns: `ok` for an accepted push and for a no-op; `refused` for a push refused by a rule, by the options stage or by the compare-and-swap; `error` for a pack failure, a timeout and `internal error; try again`.

### End-to-end flows

1. An agent with a PAT runs `git push` of a new branch to a workspace it owns, then rewrites the branch and force-pushes it. `parleyd` receives each pack into quarantine, evaluates the rules, moves the ref by compare-and-swap and writes one `parley.git.push` event per push; the second has `forced: true`.
2. A developer fast-forwards the protected default branch with an API key: accepted as a direct push, `head_sha` follows, the event has `direct: true`. The same developer then pushes the branch with a workspace-bound PAT, together with a second, unprotected branch: git prints the rule 2 message for the protected branch and `not updated: another ref in this push was refused` for the other; no ref moved and the new commits cannot be fetched.
3. An agent with a PAT limited to `docs/**` pushes a branch whose commit also changes `src/main.go`: the push is refused with `path src/main.go is outside this token's allowed paths`. The agent removes that file from the commit and pushes again: accepted.

## Design Decisions

1. **Profile: full.** Three end-to-end flows cross the git client, the processor, the engine, the repository and the event log.
2. **One engine, one ref writer, in `internal/gitserver/pushrule`.** The engine (`Evaluate`) evaluates; the ref writer (`Apply`, then its event step) applies an evaluated request (forwards, one ref transaction with the ref-updated stages, `head_sha`, fork activity, journal, events) and takes `via` and the version kind as parameters. The git server, package 21 and package 25 call the same two entry points, so the rules, the atomicity and the event cannot differ by surface. A sub-package keeps `internal/scm` from importing the whole git server.
3. **The engine takes plain facts, not components.** The caller's level, credential kind, binding and `paths`, and the workspace's facts, are passed in by the surface that already resolved them (package 17 for git). Lookups the engine cannot be given up front are narrow interfaces wired in `internal/hub/gitserver.go`: tracking branches (package 15), the carry-patch controller (package 37), the version-files lookup (packages 22 and 29), the event writer (package 52), the `head_sha` setter (package 10) and the ref-updated stages (packages 22 and 23). The fork activity recorder `ForkActivity` is not wired there: package 16 registers it from `internal/hub/fork.go`. Each has a default for a hub in which the owning package is not present: no tracking branches, no version files, and for the controller the fail-closed answer below.
4. **A `carry_patch` workspace without a registered controller is refused**, with `internal error; try again`. Allowing would be failing open (GIT-FR-033).
5. **"Owner" in the exemption is the access level `owner` of package 07.** On a task fork that is the fork's owner and the parent's owner. GIT-FR-034 says "the workspace's owner"; the access rule is the one definition of that.
6. **Rules 2, 2a and 3 apply to `refs/heads/*` only**, as their messages name a branch. Tags of the parent in a fork are not covered by rule 3 here.
7. **The hub parses the receive-pack request and writes the status report itself.** The pack goes to `git index-pack` with a quarantine object directory; refs are written with one `git update-ref --stdin` transaction carrying the expected old values, prepared before the quarantined objects are moved into the repository and committed after, so that a push that loses the compare-and-swap leaves no object behind. A ref held by another transaction at that moment counts as moved. `git receive-pack` is not run, because its report cannot carry the rules' messages for every ref and it has no place for the stages of GIT-FR-020.
8. **Rules are evaluated on the `before` the client sent; the compare-and-swap is checked when the refs are written.** A client that sends a false `before` to pass as a fast-forward is caught by the compare-and-swap.
9. **Which ref carries a rule 5 refusal.** The PRD says "the whole push". The message goes to the first update in command order from whose head the offending commit is reachable; the others get `not updated: another ref in this push was refused`.
10. **Commit order for rule 5** is oldest first, a parent before its children, as `git rev-list --reverse --topo-order` lists them; paths within a commit in byte order.
11. **Texts the PRD leaves open.** `unpack invalid pack`, `unpack pack exceeds the maximum push size`, `unpack push timed out`, the per-ref `unpacker error` (git's own wording), `origin rejected push: timed out` for a forward over 120 s, When the options stage of package 19 refuses a push, the stage's message M is the text: `ng <ref> M` per ref and `error: M` once, as package 19 specifies it (GIT-FR-051).
12. **A push with no commands answers `200` with an empty result body**: there is no ref to report on.
13. **Counting.** A compare-and-swap refusal counts as `refused` (the hub worked; the client must fetch). `internal error; try again`, a pack failure and a timeout count as `error`. The counter is package 17's: the processor returns the result through `PushProcessor` and package 17 increments, so no request is counted twice.
14. **Owed events are written at the next start only.** §14.3.6 requires exactly that; no retry runs in between.
15. **A fork's `head_sha` is not set by a push**: it is the parent's head of the fork's base branch (WS-FR-074).
16. **Versions join the ref update through stages (with packages 19, 21 and 22).** CHG-FR-010 asks for the version in the transaction of the ref update. A git ref cannot join a store transaction, so the writer prepares the ref transaction first, runs the stages in one store transaction and commits the two back to back; a stage failure therefore stops the refs from moving, and the one remaining gap (a stop between the two commits) is closed by start-up reconciliation. Package 19's mapping stage only opens changes and words the `remote:` lines; package 21 calls the same `Evaluate` and `Apply`.
17. **Branch globs are matched by package 11** (`internal/workspace/branchglob.go`). This package has no matcher of its own, so settings validation, the push rules, the source control API and landing cannot disagree on what a glob protects.
18. **Fork activity is reported by the ref writer**, once per accepted request on a fork, so that the git server and package 21 need no call of their own. The recorder is package 16's, reached through `ForkActivity`, which package 16 registers from `internal/hub/fork.go`.
19. **A land's verdict is built without `Evaluate` (with package 25).** `AllowedVerdict(updates)` in `internal/gitserver/pushrule` returns a verdict in which every update is allowed, with `created`, `deleted` and `forced` computed and `direct` false. `Apply` accepts it with `via` `land`. Why: landing has its own gates and moves protected targets; asking the engine would refuse them under rule 2.
20. **The post-push listeners are called by the ref writer, for every surface (with packages 21, 25 and 37).** The event step of the ref writer, which every caller of `Apply` runs after the ref transaction, ends by calling each registered listener on its own goroutine with the slug, the accepted updates, `via` and the session id. The git processor, package 21 and package 25 therefore send no notification of their own, and package 37 reaches API writes and lands through the one registration.
21. **The version-files lookup gets no target branch (with package 29).** Its arguments are the slug, the branch, the new head and the opens-change flag. Package 29 implements it and, for an update that opens a change, takes the target that package 22's open defaults to.
22. **`CompareAndSwapRef` and `IsAncestor` of `internal/gitrepo` are package 12's.** This package declares neither again: the repository view answers ancestry with `IsAncestor` (run over the quarantine's objects when a push has one), and the several-ref transaction in `reftx.go` reports a failed expectation with the `ErrRefMoved` of `CompareAndSwapRef`, which stays the writer of a single ref.
23. **Wiring is in `internal/hub/gitserver.go`**: process composition belongs to `internal/hub`.
24. **Project-wide:** Go; `git` 2.38 or later as a subprocess through `internal/gitrepo`, no git library; bare repositories; SQLite through `modernc.org/sqlite` behind `internal/store`; `net/http`; tests with `testing`, table-driven, `net/http/httptest`, repositories made with `git init` in `t.TempDir()`.

## Dependencies

- Package 17 `git_smart_http` (draft): the `git-receive-pack` route, the checks before the exchange, the `PushProcessor` interface with the caller and workspace it hands over, and the git request counter it keeps.
- Package 11 `workspace_read_update_settings` (draft): the branch-glob matcher in `internal/workspace/branchglob.go`.
- Package 12 `workspace_sync_from_origin` (draft): `IsAncestor` and `CompareAndSwapRef` with its `ErrRefMoved` in `internal/gitrepo`.
- Package 52 `durable_event_log_and_stream` (draft): writing events.
- Through it: package 10 `workspace_create_and_clone` (the workspace record, `internal/gitrepo`), package 07 `workspace_access_rule` (the level), package 06 `api_keys_and_access_tokens` (PATs, `paths`, the path glob matcher) and package 03 `server_lifecycle_and_configuration` (`[git]` configuration, the store, start-up).
- External: the `git` command, 2.38 or later.

## Glossary

- **Hub**: The `parleyd` server.
- **Workspace**: A repository the hub holds, identified by its `slug`. Either a registered repository or a task fork.
- **Task fork (fork)**: A workspace created from another workspace (its parent) for one task.
- **Tracking branch**: In a fork, a branch that existed in the parent at fork time. It is read-only in the fork and always equals the parent's branch.
- **Protected branch**: A branch that moves only by landing a change, by sync from origin, or by a direct fast-forward push from the workspace's owner or the admin token. Nobody can force-push or delete it. By default the default branch.
- **Direct push**: A fast-forward update of a protected branch by the workspace's owner or the admin token, over git or the source control API, without a change. Allowed while the workspace setting `protect.owner_push` is true.
- **Path-scoped token**: A PAT whose writes are limited to files matching a list of globs.
- **Bound token**: A PAT confined to one workspace (and the forks created with it).
- **Carry-patch workspace**: A workspace that tracks an upstream project and keeps an ordered list of patches on top of it.
- **Integration branch**: For a carry-patch workspace, the branch the hub rebuilds as upstream plus the ordered patches.
- **Hub event**: A record of something the hub did (`parley.*` types), with a sequence number.
- **Ref update**: One command of a push, `{ref, before, after}`; a create has an all-zero `before`, a delete an all-zero `after`.
- **Forced**: An update that is neither a create nor a delete and whose `before` is not an ancestor of `after`.
- **Quarantine**: Where the objects of a push are held until the push is accepted; a refused push's objects are discarded from it.

# Requirements

## Requirements

### REQ-1: Rule order and the decision

**Rationale:** The git server and the source control API must reach the same decision for the same write, so the order and the fail-closed answer live in one engine (GIT-FR-030, GIT-FR-033, SCM-FR-021).

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-1.1] THE push rule engine SHALL for any ref update, evaluate the rules in the order hub-owned refs, protected branches, default branch deletion, tracking branches, carry-patch push control, path-scoped tokens, and answer with the message and error_type of the first rule that refuses
   → decision {allowed: false, message: the rule's message with <branch> replaced by the ref name without refs/heads/, error_type: one of hub_owned_ref, protected_branch, default_branch, tracking_branch, integration_branch, patch_branch, path_not_allowed}
   Check: unit
   - setup: a bare repository made with git init in t.TempDir() holding branches main, dev, feat and patch/a
   - setup: stub lookups: tracking branches {main, dev} for the fork; a carry-patch controller stub with a scripted answer per ref
   ```
   in internal/gitserver/pushrule/engine_test.go, a table of updates that two rules would refuse, each run through Evaluate, asserting message and error_type: (delete of the protected default branch 'main' -> protected_branch, 'main is protected and cannot be force-pushed or deleted', not default_branch); (fork: create of 'main' that is protected and a tracking branch -> protected_branch); (fork: fast-forward of protected tracking branch 'main' by the parent's owner with an API key -> tracking_branch); (fork with protected_branches []: delete of tracking default branch 'main' -> default_branch); (carry_patch workspace: fast-forward of protected branch 'patch/a' by the owner with an API key, controller refuses with patch_branch -> patch_branch and the controller's message); (carry_patch workspace: update of 'patch/a' by an org-member-level caller, protected -> protected_branch, controller not asked); (update of unprotected 'feat' by a PAT with paths ['docs/**'] adding a commit that changes 'src/a.go' -> path_not_allowed); (fork: update of tracking branch 'dev' by the same PAT with the same commit -> tracking_branch)
   ```
1. [REQ-1.2] WHEN a ref update outside refs/parley/ is refused by no rule, THE push rule engine SHALL allow it and report whether it is a create, a delete, a forced update and a direct push
   → decision {allowed: true, created: before is all-zero, deleted: after is all-zero, forced: neither create nor delete and before is not an ancestor of after, direct: false for every ref that is not a protected branch}
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/gitserver/pushrule/engine_test.go, a table run through Evaluate with an owner-level API key caller on a repository workspace with protected_branches ['main']: create refs/heads/feat -> created; fast-forward of refs/heads/feat -> none of the flags; update of refs/heads/feat to a commit that is not a descendant -> forced; delete of refs/heads/feat -> deleted; create, move and delete of refs/tags/v1; create of refs/notes/commits; create of refs/custom/x; create of refs/heads/parley/x; create of refs/parleyx/y; every row asserts allowed == true and the four flags, with direct == false
   ```
1. [REQ-1.3] IF a rule cannot be evaluated because the workspace's settings cannot be read, an ancestry question to git fails, the tracking-branch lookup fails, the carry-patch controller reports a failure, the version-files lookup fails, or the workspace is in mode carry_patch and no controller is registered, THEN THE push rule engine SHALL refuse the ref update
   → decision {allowed: false, message: 'internal error; try again', error_type: 'internal'}; Evaluate itself returns no Go error and never a decision with allowed true for that update
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/gitserver/pushrule/engine_test.go, a table of injected faults, one per row, each on an update that would otherwise be allowed: settings reader returns an error; the repository view returns an error for is-ancestor on a protected branch; tracking lookup returns an error on a fork; controller stub returns an error on a carry_patch workspace; engine built with no controller and workspace mode carry_patch; version-files lookup returns an error for a path-scoped PAT update that adds no commit; assert message == 'internal error; try again' and error_type == 'internal' in every row
   ```
1. [REQ-1.4] THE push rule engine SHALL for any request, evaluate every ref update before anything is written, and write no ref, emit no event and start no forward to origin while evaluating
   → one decision per update in request order; the repository's refs are byte-for-byte the same after Evaluate as before it
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/gitserver/pushrule/engine_test.go: refsBefore = git for-each-ref; v = Evaluate(request with three updates: one allowed, one refused by rule 1, one on a carry_patch patch branch for which the controller stub answers allow-after-forward); assert len(v.Decisions) == 3 in request order; assert v.Refused(); assert git for-each-ref == refsBefore; assert the stub's forward function was called 0 times; assert the event writer stub was called 0 times
   ```

### REQ-2: Hub-owned refs, the default branch and tracking branches

**Rationale:** Refs the hub maintains, the branch every clone checks out and the branches a fork inherits must not be rewritten by a client (rules 1, 2a and 3 of GIT-FR-030, WS-FR-073).

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-2.1] IF a ref update names a ref under refs/parley/, whatever the credential, including the admin token, THEN THE push rule engine SHALL refuse the create, the update and the delete
   → decision {allowed: false, message: 'refs/parley/ is maintained by the hub and cannot be pushed to', error_type: 'hub_owned_ref'}
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/gitserver/pushrule/rules_test.go, a table over refs {refs/parley/changes/3/1, refs/parley/replaced/patch-a, refs/parley/sandboxes/sb1/main, refs/parley/x} x kinds {create, update, delete} x callers {admin token, owner API key, owner PAT}: assert the message and error_type hub_owned_ref in every row
   ```
1. [REQ-2.2] IF a ref update deletes the workspace's default branch and no protected_branches glob matches that branch, THEN THE push rule engine SHALL refuse the delete for every credential
   → decision {allowed: false, message: '<branch> is the default branch and cannot be deleted', error_type: 'default_branch'}
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/gitserver/pushrule/rules_test.go: workspace with default branch 'trunk' and protected_branches []; table over callers {admin token, owner API key}: delete of refs/heads/trunk -> message 'trunk is the default branch and cannot be deleted', error_type default_branch; and in the same table a forced update of refs/heads/trunk and a delete of refs/tags/trunk are allowed
   ```
1. [REQ-2.3] IF the workspace is a task fork and a ref update names a branch that the tracking-branch lookup reports as a tracking branch, THEN THE push rule engine SHALL refuse the create, the update and the delete for every credential
   → decision {allowed: false, message: '<branch> tracks the parent workspace and is read-only in this fork; push a new branch', error_type: 'tracking_branch'}
   Check: unit
   - setup: a fork workspace fact set {kind: fork, parent: demo} and a repository workspace fact set
   ```
   in internal/gitserver/pushrule/rules_test.go, with a lookup stub reporting {dev, release/1} as tracking branches of fork 'demo--k3x9w2ab' and protected_branches []: table over branches {dev, release/1} x kinds {create, update, delete} x callers {admin token, fork owner API key, fork-bound PAT} -> 'dev tracks the parent workspace and is read-only in this fork; push a new branch' with error_type tracking_branch; a create of refs/heads/task-1 in the fork is allowed; an update of refs/heads/dev on a repository workspace is allowed and the lookup is not called for it
   ```

### REQ-3: Protected branches and the owner exemption

**Rationale:** Work reaches a protected branch by landing; the owner keeps a fast-forward door that can be closed, and nobody can rewrite or delete the branch (rule 2, GIT-FR-034, GIT-FR-035, section 8.3.1).

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-3.1] THE push rule engine SHALL for any branch name and any protected_branches list, treat the branch as protected exactly when the branch-glob matcher of package 11 (internal/workspace/branchglob.go) reports that at least one glob matches the whole branch name, and use no other matcher for protected_branches
   → protected(branch, globs) is what the matcher of package 11 answers for the branch name without refs/heads/ (* is any run of characters except /, ** any run including /, case-sensitive); an empty list protects nothing; refs outside refs/heads/ are never protected
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/gitserver/pushrule/protected_test.go, with the real matcher of internal/workspace, a table of (branch, globs, want) asked through the engine's protected test: ('main',['main'],true); ('main2',['main'],false); ('mai',['main'],false); ('Main',['main'],false); ('release/1.0',['release/*'],true); ('release/1.0/hotfix',['release/*'],false); ('release/1.0/hotfix',['release/**'],true); ('a',['*'],true); ('feature/a',['*'],false); ('feature/a',['**'],true); ('x',[],false); ('dev',['main','dev'],true); ('rel-1',['rel-*'],true); and through Evaluate: a forced update of refs/tags/main with protected_branches ['main'] is allowed
   ```
1. [REQ-3.2] IF a ref update is a forced update or a delete of a protected branch, whatever the credential and whatever protect.owner_push is, THEN THE push rule engine SHALL refuse it
   → decision {allowed: false, message: '<branch> is protected and cannot be force-pushed or deleted', error_type: 'protected_branch'}
   Check: unit
   - setup: a bare repository in t.TempDir() where main has a descendant commit and an unrelated commit to push
   ```
   in internal/gitserver/pushrule/protected_test.go, one table of (caller, protect.owner_push, update kind on protected 'main', want): rows for forced update and delete x callers {admin token, owner API key, owner unbound PAT without paths, owner workspace-bound PAT} x owner_push {true, false} -> 'main is protected and cannot be force-pushed or deleted'; rows for create of 'release/2' with protected_branches ['main','release/*'] x the same callers -> 'release/2 is protected; push another branch and open a change (git push -o parley.change)'; rows for a fast-forward of 'main': (admin token, false), (owner API key, false), (member-level API key, true), (owner workspace-bound PAT, true), (owner PAT with paths ['**'], true), (member-level PAT, true) -> 'main is protected; push another branch and open a change (git push -o parley.change)'; rows for a fast-forward of 'main' with owner_push true: admin token, owner API key, owner unbound PAT without paths, and on a fork the parent's owner with an API key on the fork's own protected branch -> allowed with direct == true; every refused row asserts error_type protected_branch
   ```
1. [REQ-3.3] IF a ref update creates a branch that a protected_branches glob matches, whatever the credential, THEN THE push rule engine SHALL refuse it
   → decision {allowed: false, message: '<branch> is protected; push another branch and open a change (git push -o parley.change)', error_type: 'protected_branch'}
   Check: same as REQ-3.2
1. [REQ-3.4] IF a ref update is a fast-forward of a protected branch and protect.owner_push is false, or the caller's level is neither owner nor admin, or the credential is a workspace-bound PAT or a PAT with paths, THEN THE push rule engine SHALL refuse it
   → decision {allowed: false, message: '<branch> is protected; push another branch and open a change (git push -o parley.change)', error_type: 'protected_branch'}
   Check: same as REQ-3.2
1. [REQ-3.5] WHEN a ref update is a fast-forward of an existing protected branch, protect.owner_push is true, the caller's level is owner or admin, and the credential is an API key, the admin token or a PAT that is neither bound to a workspace nor carries paths, THE push rule engine SHALL let the update pass rule 2 and mark it as a direct push
   → decision {allowed: true, direct: true, created: false, deleted: false, forced: false}, provided rules 1, 3, 4 and 5 do not refuse it
   Check: same as REQ-3.2
1. [REQ-3.6] IF a ref update satisfies the owner exemption and names a branch that the tracking-branch rule or the carry-patch controller refuses, THEN THE push rule engine SHALL refuse it with the message and error_type of that later rule
   → decision {allowed: false, error_type: 'tracking_branch', 'integration_branch' or 'patch_branch'}; direct is not reported as true
   Check: same as REQ-1.1

### REQ-4: Carry-patch hand-off and forwarding to origin

**Rationale:** Carry-patch push control is decided elsewhere (package 37), but where it sits in the order, that its one outside effect runs last, and what its failure does to a push are part of push processing (rule 4, GIT-FR-031, GIT-FR-061).

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-4.1] WHEN a ref update on a workspace in mode carry_patch has passed rules 1 to 3, THE push rule engine SHALL ask the registered carry-patch controller once for that update and take its answer as the decision of rule 4
   → controller answers refuse -> decision {allowed: false, message: the controller's message, error_type: the controller's integration_branch or patch_branch}; allow -> the update goes on to rule 5; allow-after-forward -> the update goes on to rule 5 and, when allowed, carries a pending forward; the controller is not asked on a workspace in mode standard nor for an update that rules 1 to 3 refused
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/gitserver/pushrule/carrypatch_test.go, with a recording controller stub: table of (workspace mode, ref, scripted answer, want decision, want controller calls): (carry_patch, refs/heads/integration, refuse{'integration branch integration is maintained by the hub; push a patch branch and rebuild instead', integration_branch}, refused with that message and type, 1); (carry_patch, refs/heads/patch/a, allow, allowed without forward, 1); (carry_patch, refs/heads/patch/a, allow-after-forward, allowed with a pending forward, 1); (carry_patch, refs/parley/x, any, hub_owned_ref, 0); (standard, refs/heads/patch/a, any, allowed, 0)
   ```
1. [REQ-4.2] IF the workspace is in mode carry_patch and no carry-patch controller is registered, THEN THE push rule engine SHALL refuse every ref update that passed rules 1 to 3
   → decision {allowed: false, message: 'internal error; try again', error_type: 'internal'}
   Check: same as REQ-1.3
1. [REQ-4.3] WHEN every ref update of a request is allowed and at least one carries a pending forward, THE ref writer SHALL run the forwards after all rules have been evaluated and before any ref is written, in command order, each under a limit of 120 seconds
   → each pending forward is invoked exactly once, in command order, before the ref transaction; in a request with a refused update no forward is invoked
   Check: unit
   - setup: a bare repository in t.TempDir() with the objects of every after value present
   - setup: the ref writer built with a stub event writer
   ```
   in internal/gitserver/pushrule/apply_test.go, with forwards that append their ref and the current value of the hub ref to a log: Apply(verdict of two patch-branch updates with forwards and one plain update); assert log refs == the two refs in command order; assert every logged hub ref value == its before value (the transaction had not run); assert all three refs hold their after values afterwards; then Apply(verdict with one refused update and one forward) -> assert the log did not grow and no ref moved
   ```
1. [REQ-4.4] IF a forward to origin fails, THEN THE ref writer SHALL refuse the whole request, write no ref, run no later forward and leave earlier forwards of the same request as they are
   → the failed update: {allowed: false, message: the message the forward returned, error_type: 'patch_branch'}; every other update: message 'not updated: another ref in this push was refused'; no ref of the hub changed; no event written
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/gitserver/pushrule/apply_test.go: three updates with forwards f1 (succeeds), f2 (fails with 'origin rejected push: non-fast-forward'), f3; r = Apply(...); assert r.Refused; assert r.Updates[1].Message == 'origin rejected push: non-fast-forward' and error_type == 'patch_branch'; assert r.Updates[0].Message == r.Updates[2].Message == 'not updated: another ref in this push was refused'; assert f1 called once, f3 called 0 times, no undo call recorded for f1; assert git for-each-ref unchanged; assert event writer stub calls == 0
   ```
1. [REQ-4.5] IF a forward to origin has not finished when its 120 second limit passes, THEN THE ref writer SHALL cancel that forward and refuse the whole request
   → the update: {allowed: false, message: 'origin rejected push: timed out', error_type: 'patch_branch'}; the forward's context is cancelled; no ref of the hub changed
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/gitserver/pushrule/apply_test.go, with the ref writer's forward limit set to 50 ms through its test option and a forward that blocks until its context is done: r = Apply(...); assert r.Updates[0].Message == 'origin rejected push: timed out'; assert the forward observed ctx.Err() != nil; assert git for-each-ref unchanged; and assert the production default of the limit == 120 s
   ```
1. [REQ-4.6] WHEN the ref writer has finished an accepted request, whatever its surface: a git push, a write through the source control API or a land, THE ref writer SHALL report the workspace, the moved refs in command order, via and the session id to every registered post-push listener in the background
   → each listener is called once with the slug, the accepted updates, via ('git', 'api' or 'land' as the caller of Apply passed it) and the session id of the request, or null; the call is made by the ref writer's event step, so the git processor, package 21 and package 25 make none of their own; the caller's answer is complete while a listener is still running; a listener that returns an error or panics changes neither the answer nor the refs; no listener is called for a refused request or a push with no commands
   Check: integration
   - setup: a bare repository in t.TempDir(), a migrated store and the ref writer with two listeners registered: A, which records its arguments and blocks on a channel, and B, which panics
   - setup: the push processor mounted on net/http/httptest over the same repository
   ```
   in internal/gitserver/pushrule/event_test.go, a table over (via, session) {('git', 's-1'); ('api', 's-2'); ('land', null)}: run Apply and its event step for a verdict of one create; assert the event step returned while A is still blocked; release A; assert A received ('demo', [the create], via, session) exactly once per row; assert the process did not crash and the ref holds its after value; Apply(a verdict with a refused update) -> assert A's call count unchanged; and in internal/gitserver/receive_test.go: resp = push(create refs/heads/feat); assert resp is fully read with 'ok refs/heads/feat' while A is still blocked and A received via 'git'; a request with no commands -> assert no further call
   ```

### REQ-5: Path-scoped tokens

**Rationale:** An operator bounds an agent's write access by paths; the bound must hold for every commit the agent adds and must not be dodged by adopting commits made with another credential (rule 5, GIT-FR-032, LAND-FR-080).

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-5.1] IF the caller's credential is a PAT with paths, every ref update passed rules 1 to 4, and a commit that is new to the repository changes a path that matches none of the token's globs, THEN THE push rule engine SHALL refuse the whole request and name the first offending path
   → the first update in command order from whose after value the offending commit is reachable: {allowed: false, message: 'path <path> is outside this token's allowed paths', error_type: 'path_not_allowed', path: <path>}; the verdict as a whole is refused
   Check: unit
   - setup: a bare repository in t.TempDir() with branches main, feat and other; for the fork row a second bare repository acting as the parent whose refs the repository view includes
   - setup: the glob matcher of package 06 used unstubbed
   ```
   in internal/gitserver/pushrule/paths_test.go, a table of pushes by a PAT with paths ['docs/**'], each built with git in the test repository and run through Evaluate, (case, want): (commit changes docs/a.md -> allowed); (commit changes docs/a.md and src/main.go -> path src/main.go); (older commit changes zz/late.txt, newer commit changes aa/first.txt -> path zz/late.txt); (one commit changes b.txt and a.txt -> path a.txt); (commit renames docs/a.md to src/a.md -> path src/a.md); (commit renames src/x.md to docs/x.md -> path src/x.md); (new root commit on a new branch with docs/a.md and other/b.md -> path other/b.md); (merge commit whose first-parent diff is docs/m.md and whose second parent, already in the repository, changed src/s.go -> allowed); (force-push of a branch rebased onto a newer main whose existing commits changed src/** and whose own commit changes docs/r.md -> allowed); (fork: pushed head contains commits that only the parent repository's refs reach and that changed src/** plus one own commit changing docs/f.md -> allowed); (annotated tag refs/tags/v1 pointing to a new commit that changes src/t.go -> path src/t.go); (refs/notes/commits with a new commit that changes a file named by a commit id -> path that file); (delete of refs/heads/feat -> allowed); (fast-forward of refs/heads/feat to a commit already reachable from refs/heads/other, no change lookup registered -> allowed); (two updates, the second head carrying the offending commit -> the second decision carries the message and the first is allowed); in every refused row assert error_type == 'path_not_allowed' and the path field
   ```
1. [REQ-5.2] THE push rule engine SHALL for any request by a PAT with paths, check exactly the commits reachable from the pushed after values and not reachable from any ref the repository had before the push, including the parent's refs in a task fork, comparing each commit with its first parent, a root commit with the empty tree, and counting a rename with both its old and its new path
   → commits already in the repository or in the fork's parent are never the reason for a refusal; tags, notes and other refs are checked like branches
   Check: same as REQ-5.1
1. [REQ-5.3] THE push rule engine SHALL for any refused path check, name the first offending path taking the checked commits oldest first, a parent before its children, and the paths within one commit in byte order
   → the path in the message and in the path field is the same for the same pushed commits on every evaluation
   Check: same as REQ-5.1
1. [REQ-5.4] WHEN a PAT with paths pushes a delete, or an update that adds no new commit to a branch for which the version-files lookup reports no version, THE push rule engine SHALL allow the update under rule 5
   → decision {allowed: true}
   Check: same as REQ-5.1
1. [REQ-5.5] IF a PAT with paths pushes an update that adds no new commit, and the version-files lookup reports that the branch is the source of a draft or open change, or that the push opens one, with a file among the resulting version's files against its base that matches none of the token's globs, THEN THE push rule engine SHALL refuse the whole request and name the first such file in byte order
   → decision {allowed: false, message: 'path <path> is outside this token's allowed paths', error_type: 'path_not_allowed', path: <path>}
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/gitserver/pushrule/paths_test.go, with a version-files lookup stub and a fast-forward of refs/heads/feat to a commit already in the repository, PAT paths ['docs/**']: lookup reports files ['src/x.go','docs/a.md','lib/y.go'] -> refused with path lib/y.go; lookup reports files ['docs/a.md'] -> allowed; lookup reports no version -> allowed; assert the lookup received exactly the workspace slug, the branch, the after value and the opens-change flag the request carried, and no target branch, also in a row whose flag says the update opens a change
   ```
1. [REQ-5.6] WHEN the caller's credential is an API key, the admin token or a PAT without paths, THE push rule engine SHALL skip rule 5 without reading any commit
   → decision {allowed: true} for an update that rules 1 to 4 pass, whatever paths its commits change; the repository view receives no new-commits or changed-files question
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/gitserver/pushrule/paths_test.go, with a counting repository view: table over callers {owner API key, admin token, PAT with paths null}: Evaluate(update adding a commit that changes src/main.go) -> allowed; assert the view's new-commits call count == 0
   ```

### REQ-6: Push processing over git-receive-pack

**Rationale:** A push either lands whole or leaves no trace, and a stock git client must be told why in the two places it looks (GIT-FR-020 to GIT-FR-027, section 5.7).

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-6.1] WHEN a git client sends a git-receive-pack request in which every ref update passes the rules and the compare-and-swap, THE push processor SHALL update all refs of the request together, keep the pushed objects in the repository and answer with the status report
   → HTTP 200, Content-Type application/x-git-receive-pack-result, a report 'unpack ok' followed by 'ok <ref>' per command in command order; every ref holds its after value (a deleted ref is gone); every pushed object is readable in the repository
   Check: integration
   - setup: the push processor mounted on net/http/httptest over a bare repository in t.TempDir(), with the real rule engine, the real ref writer and an owner-level API key caller
   - setup: client capabilities report-status, side-band-64k, delete-refs, atomic unless a row says otherwise

### REQ-7: Compare-and-swap of refs

**Rationale:** No request fails only because another operation is running; writers of the same ref are ordered by compare-and-swap instead of locks (GIT-FR-022, PLAT-FR-019).

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-7.1] IF a ref update's before value is not the ref's current value: the ref has moved, the update creates a ref that exists, or it updates or deletes a ref that is missing, THEN THE ref writer SHALL refuse the whole request and write no ref
   → the mismatching update: {allowed: false, message: 'ref changed since it was read; fetch and try again', outcome: ref_moved}; every other update: message 'not updated: another ref in this push was refused'; all refs unchanged; no event
   Check: unit
   - setup: a bare repository in t.TempDir() with refs/heads/feat two commits ahead of the stale before value
   ```
   in internal/gitserver/pushrule/apply_test.go, a table of single mismatches, each applied in a request together with a valid create of refs/heads/ok: update of refs/heads/feat with before == an older commit; create of refs/heads/feat which exists; update of refs/heads/gone which does not exist; delete of refs/heads/gone; delete of refs/heads/feat with a wrong before; assert the result is refused with outcome ref_moved, the message on the mismatching update and the not-updated message on refs/heads/ok; assert git for-each-ref unchanged (refs/heads/ok was not created); assert event writer stub calls == 0
   ```
1. [REQ-7.2] WHEN two or more requests update the same ref from the same before value at the same time, THE push processor SHALL apply exactly one of them and refuse the others
   → exactly one request answers 'ok <ref>'; each other answers 'ng <ref> ref changed since it was read; fetch and try again'; the ref holds the winner's after value
   Check: integration
   ```
   in internal/gitserver/receive_test.go: eight goroutines each post a fast-forward of refs/heads/feat from the same before to its own distinct commit, released together; assert count of 'ok refs/heads/feat' == 1 and count of 'ng refs/heads/feat ref changed since it was read; fetch and try again' == 7; assert git rev-parse refs/heads/feat == the winner's after; assert the seven losers' commits are not readable in the repository
   ```
1. [REQ-7.3] WHEN requests that update different refs of one workspace run at the same time, THE push processor SHALL apply each of them without waiting for the other
   → every request answers 'ok <ref>'; a request completes while another request on the same workspace is still held in a stage
   Check: integration
   ```
   in internal/gitserver/receive_test.go: request A creates refs/heads/a and is held inside a mapping stage that blocks on a channel; request B creates refs/heads/b; assert B's response 'ok refs/heads/b' is read while A is still blocked; release A; assert A answers 'ok refs/heads/a'; assert both refs exist
   ```
1. [REQ-7.4] WHEN every ref update of a request passed the rules, its ref transaction is prepared, and ref-updated stages are registered with the ref writer, THE ref writer SHALL run each registered stage once, in registration order, inside the commit step: in one store transaction the ref writer opens, after the compare-and-swap is verified and before the refs take their new values, and commit that store transaction directly after the ref transaction
   → each stage is called once with the store transaction, the workspace facts, the caller facts with the credential type and id, the session id, via, the version kind the caller of Apply named (push, commit, ref, rebase or none) and the accepted updates with their flags; at call time every ref still holds its before value and the new objects are readable in the repository; rows a stage wrote in the transaction are stored when Apply returns; the result of each update carries the version {workspace_slug, number, version} a stage reported for it, or none; no stage is called for a refused request
   Check: unit
   - setup: a bare repository in t.TempDir() and a migrated store; two recording stages registered with the ref writer, the first writing one row in the transaction it is given and reporting version {demo, 4, 2} for refs/heads/feat
   ```
   in internal/gitserver/pushrule/apply_test.go: Apply(verdict of update refs/heads/feat and create refs/heads/other, via 'api', version kind 'commit', session 's1', caller with credential id 'k1'); assert the stages were called once each in registration order with via 'api', kind 'commit', session 's1', credential id 'k1' and both updates; assert each stage saw refs/heads/feat at its before value and could read the after commit; assert after Apply the ref holds after and the stage's row is stored; assert result[refs/heads/feat].version == {demo, 4, 2} and result[refs/heads/other].version is none; Apply(a verdict with a refused update) -> assert no stage call
   ```
1. [REQ-7.5] IF a ref-updated stage returns an error, THEN THE ref writer SHALL abort the ref transaction, roll the store transaction back, call no later stage and refuse the whole request
   → Apply returns the stage's error unchanged beside the results; every update: {allowed: false, message: 'internal error; try again', error_type: 'internal'}; all refs unchanged; no row of any stage is stored; the journal entry is removed; no event; over git every ref is reported 'ng <ref> internal error; try again' and the request counts as error
   Check: unit
   - setup: a bare repository in t.TempDir() and a migrated store; a first stage that writes one row and a second stage that returns an error value E; a third recording stage
   ```
   in internal/gitserver/pushrule/apply_test.go: res, err = Apply(verdict of one update of refs/heads/feat, via 'git', version kind 'push'); assert err is E; assert every result has allowed == false, message 'internal error; try again' and error_type 'internal'; assert git for-each-ref unchanged; assert the first stage's row is absent; assert the third stage was not called; assert the journal is empty and the event writer stub has no call
   ```
1. [REQ-7.6] WHEN an accepted request with via git or api has written at least one ref of a task fork, THE ref writer SHALL report the fork's slug once to the registered fork activity recorder after the refs are written
   → the recorder (the interface ForkActivity of internal/gitserver/pushrule, which package 16 registers) is called once with the fork's slug; it is not called for a repository workspace, for a refused request or for via land; a recorder error is logged and changes neither the result nor the refs; with no recorder registered nothing happens

1. [REQ-7.7] WHEN a caller hands Apply, with via land, a verdict it built with AllowedVerdict instead of Evaluate, THE ref writer SHALL write the updates of that verdict as an accepted request without asking the rule engine
   → AllowedVerdict(updates) returns a verdict in which every update is allowed, with created, deleted and forced computed as Evaluate computes them and direct false; Apply with via land moves a branch that protected_branches matches, also when protect.owner_push is false, and calls no rule and no collaborator of the engine; the compare-and-swap still decides (a moved ref answers ref_moved and writes nothing); the ref-updated stages run with via land; the event has via 'land' and direct false
