### REQ-8: The parley.git.push event

**Rationale:** Consumers of the event stream follow what agents do one ref update at a time, and an accepted update must not go unrecorded because the hub stopped at the wrong moment (GIT-FR-060, GIT-FR-035, sections 5.8 and 14.3.6).

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-8.1] WHEN the refs of an accepted request have been written, THE ref writer SHALL write one parley.git.push event per updated ref, in command order
   → each event: type 'parley.git.push', resource_type 'ref', resource_id the full ref name, action 'push', workspace the slug the request named (the fork's slug for a fork), actor_type 'pat', 'api_key' or 'admin_token' after the credential, session_id the id the options stage set or null, metadata {ref, before, after, created, deleted, forced, direct, via}; before is null for a create and after is null for a delete, otherwise 40 hexadecimal characters; direct is true only for a protected branch moved under the owner exemption; via is 'git' for a push
   Check: integration
   - setup: the push processor over a bare repository in t.TempDir() and the event component of internal/event unstubbed
   ```
   in internal/gitserver/push_event_test.go, pushing through the processor with the real event log over a store in t.TempDir() and reading the workspace's events back: table of (caller, update, want metadata): (PAT, create refs/heads/feat, before null, created true, others false); (PAT, fast-forward, all flags false); (PAT, forced update, forced true); (API key, delete, after null, deleted true); (owner API key, fast-forward of protected main, direct true); (admin token, create refs/tags/v1, created true); assert one event per update with type, resource_type 'ref', resource_id == ref, action 'push', via 'git', actor_type per caller, workspace 'demo'; push to fork fact set 'demo--k3x9w2ab' -> workspace == 'demo--k3x9w2ab'; with an options stage that sets session 's-1' -> session_id == 's-1', otherwise null; a request with three commands -> three events in command order
   ```
1. [REQ-8.2] THE ref writer SHALL for any accepted request with several ref updates, write its events in one store transaction so that they hold consecutive positions among the workspace's events
   → between the first and the last event of one request no other event of the same workspace appears, also when other requests on that workspace are accepted at the same time
   Check: integration
   ```
   in internal/gitserver/push_event_test.go: six goroutines each push one request creating three refs with a distinct prefix (refs/heads/g<i>/a, /b, /c), released together; read the workspace's events in order; assert 18 events; assert that the events of each prefix occupy three adjacent positions in command order a, b, c
   ```
1. [REQ-8.3] WHEN the source control API or a land applies ref updates through the ref writer and names its surface, THE ref writer SHALL write the same event with via set to that surface
   → metadata.via == 'api' or 'land' as passed; every other field as for a push; a via value other than 'git', 'api' and 'land' is refused with an error before any ref is written; the git server, package 21 and package 25 all call the same Apply
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/gitserver/pushrule/event_test.go: table over via {'git','api','land'}: Apply(verdict of one create, via) with a capturing event writer -> assert event.metadata.via == via and the other fields; Apply(..., via 'cli') -> assert an error is returned, git for-each-ref unchanged and no event captured
   ```
1. [REQ-8.4] IF a request is refused, fails at the pack, or has no commands, THEN THE ref writer SHALL write no event
   → the workspace's event count is unchanged
   Check: same as REQ-6.2
1. [REQ-8.5] IF the event write fails after the refs of a request have been written, THEN THE ref writer SHALL complete the request as accepted and keep its journal entry
   → the result is accepted ('ok <ref>' over git); every ref holds its after value; the journal still holds the request's entry with every ref update, the actor, the session id and via
   Check: unit
   - setup: a store in t.TempDir() with the journal migration applied
   ```
   in internal/gitserver/pushrule/journal_test.go, with an event writer that returns an error: r = Apply(verdict of two creates, via 'git'); assert !r.Refused and r.Err == nil; assert both refs hold after; assert the journal has one entry listing both updates in command order with actor_type, session id and via
   ```
1. [REQ-8.6] WHEN the hub starts and the journal holds entries, THE ref writer SHALL before serving requests, write the events of every entry whose refs hold their after values, drop every entry whose refs were never written, and remove each handled entry in the same transaction as its events
   → after start-up: exactly one parley.git.push event per ref update of an entry of the first kind, with the fields the original request would have written; no event for an entry of the second kind; the journal is empty; running the reconciliation again writes nothing
   Check: integration
   ```
   in internal/gitserver/pushrule/journal_test.go, with the real event log: seed the journal with entry E1 (two updates; set the repository's refs to their after values with git update-ref), entry E2 (one create; ref absent), entry E3 (one delete whose ref is already gone); Reconcile(); assert events == E1's two in command order then E3's one, with before/after/created/deleted, actor_type, session id and via from the entries; assert no event for E2; assert the journal is empty; Reconcile() again -> assert event count unchanged; and assert the reconciliation is registered to run in parleyd's start-up before the listener accepts requests by starting the in-process hub over the seeded store and reading the events on the first request
   ```

### REQ-9: Limits, timeout and counting

**Rationale:** An operator bounds what one push may cost and sees in the metrics how pushes end (GIT-FR-002, GIT-FR-024, GIT-FR-062, section 5.9).

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-9.1] IF [git].max_push_size is greater than 0 and the pack of a push is larger than it, THEN THE push processor SHALL fail the push and change nothing
   → HTTP 200; report 'unpack pack exceeds the maximum push size' and 'ng <ref> unpacker error' per command; refs unchanged; no pushed object readable; no event; a pack of exactly the limit is accepted; with the limit 0 a pack of any size is accepted, also one larger than [server].max_body_size
   Check: integration
   ```
   in internal/gitserver/limits_test.go, with a pack of N bytes: table of (max_push_size, want): (N, 'ok refs/heads/feat'); (N-1, ['unpack pack exceeds the maximum push size', 'ng refs/heads/feat unpacker error'], refs unchanged, no quarantine directory, event count 0); (0, ok); and (0 with the server body limit set to 1 KiB and a pack over 1 KiB, ok)
   ```
1. [REQ-9.2] IF [git].timeout passes before the ref transaction of a push has started, THEN THE push processor SHALL abandon the push and change nothing
   → report 'unpack push timed out' and 'ng <ref> unpacker error' per command when the client can still be answered; refs unchanged; the quarantine directory is removed; no event; the git subprocesses of the push are no longer running
   Check: integration
   ```
   in internal/gitserver/limits_test.go, with [git].timeout 100 ms: (a) an options stage that blocks until its context is done; (b) a request body that delivers half the pack and then stalls; for each: assert the handler returns within 2 s; assert the report holds 'unpack push timed out' in case (a); assert git for-each-ref unchanged; assert no quarantine directory; assert event count == 0; and with the default configuration assert the processor's limit == 30 minutes
   ```
1. [REQ-9.3] WHEN the processor has finished a git-receive-pack request, THE push processor SHALL return its result to the git server of package 17, which counts the request once in parley_git_requests_total with service receive-pack
   → result 'ok' for an accepted push and for a push with no commands; 'refused' for a push refused by a rule, by the options stage or by the compare-and-swap; 'error' for a pack failure, a timeout and a push refused with 'internal error; try again'; exactly one increment per request, made by the handler of package 17 from the returned result; the processor increments no counter itself
   Check: integration
   ```
   in internal/gitserver/limits_test.go, sending each request through the git-receive-pack route of package 17 with the processor installed and reading the counter before and after it, a table of (request, want label): (create refs/heads/feat, ok); (flush only, ok); (create refs/parley/x, refused); (options stage refuses, refused); (stale before, refused); (truncated pack, error); (pack over max_push_size, error); (timeout, error); (settings reader fails, error); assert the delta of {service='receive-pack', result=want} == 1 and the delta of the two other results == 0
   ```

## Execution Paths

### PATH-1: An agent pushes a new branch and then force-pushes it

1. **agent** commits on a new branch in a clone of workspace 'demo' and runs git push origin fix-retry with a PAT that has git:write
2. **git client** sends the create of refs/heads/fix-retry and its pack to POST /git/acme/demo.git/git-receive-pack
3. **parleyd** receives the pack into quarantine, evaluates the push rules, creates the ref by compare-and-swap, writes one parley.git.push event with created true and answers 'ok refs/heads/fix-retry'
4. **agent** amends the commit and runs git push --force origin fix-retry
5. **parleyd** allows the forced update of the unprotected branch, moves the ref and writes a second event with forced true
6. **git client** prints the forced update and exits 0

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** a stock git client, the git routes and authentication of internal/gitserver, the push processor, rule engine and ref writer, internal/gitrepo with the git command, the event log of internal/event, the SQLite store

**Setup:**

- a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 with a data directory in t.TempDir()
- workspace 'demo' in organization 'acme', status ready, default branch main, owned by a user with a PAT carrying git:write
- a local clone made with git clone over the hub's git URL

**End state:**

- refs/heads/fix-retry in the hub's repository equals the amended commit
- the first commit of the branch is still readable in the repository
- the workspace's events hold two parley.git.push events for refs/heads/fix-retry: the first with created true and before null, the second with forced true, both with via git and actor_type pat

**Pseudocode:**

```
in internal/gitserver/push_integration_test.go: start the hub; clone; commit; run git push origin fix-retry with the PAT as Basic password; assert exit 0; amend; run git push --force origin fix-retry; assert exit 0; assert hub git rev-parse refs/heads/fix-retry == local HEAD; evs = events of 'demo' of type parley.git.push; assert len(evs) == 2 and evs[0].metadata.created and evs[1].metadata.forced
```

### PATH-2: A developer pushes a protected branch directly and is refused with a bound token

1. **developer** runs git push origin main with an API key, fast-forwarding the protected default branch of the workspace the developer owns
2. **parleyd** applies the owner exemption, moves refs/heads/main, sets the workspace's head_sha and writes a parley.git.push event with direct true
3. **developer** commits again and runs git push origin main feature-x with a PAT bound to the workspace
4. **parleyd** refuses refs/heads/main under rule 2, updates no ref, discards the pushed objects and reports both refs
5. **git client** prints '! [remote rejected] main -> main (main is protected; push another branch and open a change (git push -o parley.change))', the not-updated message for feature-x and the remote: error line, and exits with a non-zero code

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** a stock git client, the git routes and authentication of internal/gitserver, the push processor, rule engine and ref writer, the workspace record and settings of internal/workspace, internal/gitrepo with the git command, the event log of internal/event, the SQLite store

**Setup:**

- a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 with a data directory in t.TempDir()
- workspace 'demo' in organization 'acme' with default settings (protected_branches [main], protect.owner_push true), owned by a user with an API key and a PAT bound to 'demo' with git:write
- a local clone

**End state:**

- after the first push: refs/heads/main and the workspace's head_sha equal the pushed commit, and one parley.git.push event has direct true
- after the second push: git exited non-zero and its stderr holds the rule 2 message for main, 'not updated: another ref in this push was refused' for feature-x and a line starting 'remote: error: refs/heads/main:'
- refs/heads/main is still the first pushed commit, refs/heads/feature-x does not exist, git fetch of the second commit's id fails, and no further event was written

**Pseudocode:**

```
in internal/gitserver/push_integration_test.go: push main with the API key; assert exit 0; assert workspace.head_sha == pushed id; assert last event.metadata.direct; commit; out, code = git push origin main feature-x with the bound PAT; assert code != 0; assert out contains the three texts; assert hub refs unchanged; assert git fetch origin <second commit id> fails; assert event count unchanged
```

### PATH-3: An agent with a path-scoped token is held to its paths

1. **agent** commits changes to docs/guide.md and src/main.go on a new branch and runs git push origin docs-fix with a PAT whose paths are ['docs/**']
2. **parleyd** finds src/main.go among the files changed by the new commit, refuses the whole push with 'path src/main.go is outside this token's allowed paths' and discards the pushed objects
3. **git client** prints the remote rejection with that message and exits with a non-zero code
4. **agent** amends the commit to change only docs/guide.md and pushes again
5. **parleyd** finds every changed path matched by docs/**, creates the ref and writes one parley.git.push event

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** a stock git client, the git routes and authentication of internal/gitserver, the push processor, rule engine and ref writer, the token store and glob matcher of internal/identity, internal/gitrepo with the git command, the event log of internal/event, the SQLite store

**Setup:**

- a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 with a data directory in t.TempDir()
- workspace 'demo' whose main already holds src/main.go and docs/guide.md, owned by a user with a PAT carrying git:write and paths ['docs/**']
- a local clone

**End state:**

- the first push exited non-zero with 'path src/main.go is outside this token's allowed paths' in git's output, refs/heads/docs-fix absent and no event written
- the second push exited 0, refs/heads/docs-fix equals the amended commit, and exactly one parley.git.push event exists for it

**Pseudocode:**

```
in internal/gitserver/push_integration_test.go: out, code = git push origin docs-fix with the path-scoped PAT; assert code != 0 and out contains the message; assert hub has no refs/heads/docs-fix; assert event count == 0; amend to docs only; push; assert exit 0; assert hub ref == local HEAD; assert event count == 1
```


# Tasks

## Test Commands

- **all_tests:** `go test ./... -count=1`
- **linter:** `golangci-lint run ./...`
- **spec_tests:** `go test ./internal/gitserver/... ./internal/gitrepo/... -count=1`

## Dependencies

- `11` — uses its single branch-glob matcher in internal/workspace/branchglob.go to decide which branches protected_branches protects
- `12` — uses IsAncestor of internal/gitrepo for the ancestry questions of the rules, and the ErrRefMoved of its CompareAndSwapRef as the mismatch error of the several-ref transaction, instead of declaring either again
- `17` — implements the PushProcessor interface that package declares for the git-receive-pack hand-off, starts from the caller and workspace facts it hands over, and returns the result its request counter counts
- `52` — emits its hub events through the event log component

## Tasks

### 1. Build the rule engine with the rules for hub-owned refs, the default branch and tracking branches (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-1.2, REQ-1.4, REQ-2

**Steps:**

- 1.1 Add the behaviours of this task to engine_test.go and rules_test.go as table-driven tests over a bare repository made with git init in t.TempDir(), and confirm they fail
- 1.2 Define the engine's input: the workspace facts (slug, kind, parent, default branch, mode, effective protected_branches and protect.owner_push, read through a settings reader that can fail), the caller facts (level admin, owner or member; credential kind admin_token, api_key or pat; the credential id and the user id; bound or not; paths or none), the ordered ref updates {ref, before, after}, an opens-change flag per update, and a repository view that answers is-ancestor with IsAncestor of internal/gitrepo (package 12; declare no second ancestry test, and give the call the quarantine's object directory when the view has one) and can read objects held in a quarantine
- 1.3 Define the output: one decision per update in request order, allowed with created, deleted, forced and direct, or refused with message, error_type and optional path; and a verdict that reports whether any update is refused
- 1.4 Compute created from an all-zero before, deleted from an all-zero after, and forced as neither create nor delete with before not an ancestor of after
- 1.5 Evaluate the rules as an ordered list in which the first refusal decides, with empty slots for rules 2, 4 and 5 that later tasks fill; an update no rule refuses is allowed in every namespace outside refs/parley/
- 1.6 Rule 1: refuse create, update and delete of any ref under refs/parley/ for every caller, with the message of the PRD and error_type hub_owned_ref; refs/parleyx/ and refs/heads/parley/ are not hub-owned
- 1.7 Rule 2a: refuse the delete of refs/heads/<default branch> with '<branch> is the default branch and cannot be deleted' and error_type default_branch
- 1.8 Rule 3: on a workspace of kind fork, ask the tracking-branch lookup interface for the branch and refuse create, update and delete with the tracking message and error_type tracking_branch; do not call the lookup on a repository workspace; the default lookup reports no tracking branches
- 1.9 Keep evaluation free of effects: it writes no ref, calls no event writer and invokes no forward

**Touches:**

- `internal/gitserver/pushrule/engine.go`
- `internal/gitserver/pushrule/rules.go`
- `internal/gitserver/pushrule/engine_test.go`
- `internal/gitserver/pushrule/rules_test.go`

**Done when:**

- the checks of the criteria listed above exist as tests, are executable and pass
- `go test ./... -count=1` passes
- `golangci-lint run ./...` passes

### 5. Write all refs of a request in one compare-and-swap transaction with its ref-updated stages (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-7.1, REQ-7.4, REQ-7.5, REQ-7.6, REQ-7.7

**Depends on:** 1

**Steps:**

- 5.1 Add the mismatch table, the stage behaviours and the fork activity table to apply_test.go and a transaction test to internal/gitrepo/reftx_test.go and confirm they fail
- 5.2 Add to internal/gitrepo a ref transaction over a list of {ref, expected old value, new value}, run as one git update-ref --stdin transaction in two phases: prepare verifies every expected value and reports which ref failed it with the ErrRefMoved that package 12 declares for CompareAndSwapRef, the single-ref writer this transaction does not replace or redeclare (a moved ref, a create of an existing ref, an update or delete of a missing ref, or a ref another transaction holds at that moment), commit then applies all; an abort applies none; it can read new objects from a quarantine
- 5.3 Let Apply take an optional hook that runs between prepare and commit, so that the push processor can move quarantined objects into the repository only once the transaction is certain to commit
- 5.4 Add the ref writer entry point Apply, the one writer the git server, package 21 and package 25 call: it takes a verdict, the repository, the workspace and caller facts, an optional session id, via and a version kind (push, commit, ref, rebase or none), and returns per-update results, each with the version {workspace_slug, number, version} a ref-updated stage reported for it or none; export AllowedVerdict(updates), which builds a verdict that allows every update (created, deleted and forced computed, direct false) without Evaluate, and accept it in Apply with via land, so that package 25 moves a protected target without the rule engine being asked
- 5.5 Add RegisterRefUpdatedStage: a stage receives a store transaction, the workspace facts, the caller facts, the session id, via, the version kind and the accepted updates with their flags, and returns per-update versions or an error; package 22 registers the stage that records versions and package 23 the one that notes target moves
- 5.6 Build the commit step of Apply: prepare the ref transaction, run the optional hook, begin one store transaction, run the stages in registration order, commit the ref transaction, then commit the store transaction; when a stage fails abort the ref transaction, roll back, refuse every update with 'internal error; try again' and return the stage's error; when only the store commit fails after the refs moved, log it and report the request accepted (the start-up reconciliation of package 23 records the missed version)
- 5.7 When the verdict has a refused update, write nothing and give every other update the message 'not updated: another ref in this push was refused'
- 5.8 When the transaction reports a mismatch, return outcome ref_moved with 'ref changed since it was read; fetch and try again' on the mismatching update and the not-updated message on the others
- 5.9 Take no lock that spans a request: two Apply calls on one repository are ordered only by the transaction
- 5.10 After a successful transaction on a repository workspace whose default branch moved, call the head_sha setter interface with the slug and the new id; do not call it for a fork
- 5.11 Declare the interface ForkActivity (one operation: record activity for a fork slug) with a registration function that package 16 calls from internal/hub/fork.go; after a successful transaction with via git or api on a task fork call it once with the fork's slug, log an error and go on

### 7. Process a push behind git-receive-pack (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-6, REQ-7.2, REQ-7.3

**Depends on:** 4, 6

**Steps:**

- 7.1 Add the behaviours of this task to internal/gitserver/receive_test.go with a pkt-line request builder and a report parser as test helpers, and confirm they fail
- 7.2 Add to internal/gitrepo a quarantine: a temporary object directory beside the repository into which git index-pack writes the pack with the repository's objects as alternates, a repository view over both, a migrate step that moves the objects into the repository, and a discard step that removes the directory; verify that every command's after value resolves to an object
- 7.3 Parse the request: the command list with the client's capabilities (report-status, side-band-64k, delete-refs, atomic, push-options), then the push options when announced, then the pack; a gzip request body is read through its decoder; a request with no commands is answered 200 with an empty body and nothing else runs
- 7.4 Run the stages in order: options stage, pack into quarantine (skipped for a request of deletes only), Evaluate over the quarantine view, Apply (forwards, prepare the ref transaction, migrate the quarantine, commit, head_sha), mapping stage, answer; define the options stage and the mapping stage as interfaces package 19 registers, with defaults that accept every option and add no line; pass Apply via git and version kind push
- 7.5 Let the options stage refuse the push with a message M before any pack byte is stored: read the rest of the body and discard it, report 'unpack ok' and 'ng <ref> M' for every ref, send the one side-band line 'error: M', write nothing; let the stage set the session id that Apply receives
- 7.6 Write the status report: 'unpack ok' and 'ok <ref>' per command for an accepted push; for a refused push 'unpack ok', 'ng <ref> <message>' per ref and a side-band line 'error: <ref>: <message>' per refused ref (not for the not-updated refs); always HTTP 200 with Content-Type application/x-git-receive-pack-result
- 7.7 On a pack that git index-pack rejects, an empty body where a pack is due, or an after value that names no object, report 'unpack invalid pack' and 'ng <ref> unpacker error' per command
- 7.8 Discard the quarantine on every outcome except an accepted push, so that a refused push's objects are never readable in the repository and no directory is left behind
- 7.9 Send the lines the mapping stage returns on the side band, after the refs are written; pass it the accepted updates with their direct flags and the version each ref-updated stage reported
- 7.10 Send only what the client asked for: no report without report-status, no side-band framing and no 'error:' lines without side-band-64k
- 7.11 Call no post-push listener from the processor: the event step of the ref writer calls them for every surface (task 8); run that step after the mapping stage and do not wait for the listeners before the response is written
- 7.12 Implement the interface PushProcessor that package 17 declares in internal/gitserver/push.go with this processor: take the caller facts and the workspace record it hands over, turn them into the engine's workspace and caller facts, write the whole response and return ok, refused or error; pass the processor to the handler of package 17 and wire the engine, the ref writer and their collaborators in internal/hub/gitserver.go

### 8. Record every accepted ref update as a parley.git.push event (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-8, REQ-4.6

**Depends on:** 7

**Steps:**

- 8.1 Add the behaviours of this task to internal/gitserver/push_event_test.go, internal/gitserver/pushrule/event_test.go and journal_test.go and confirm they fail
- 8.2 Register a store migration for the journal: one entry per request with the workspace slug, the ordered ref updates with their flags, actor type and actor id, credential id, session id and via
- 8.3 In Apply, accept only via 'git', 'api' or 'land' and return an error before any effect for another value
- 8.4 Write the journal entry in its own transaction after the forwards and before the ref transaction; remove it when the ref transaction refuses
- 8.5 Give the ref writer a second step that the caller runs after the ref transaction, so that the push processor can run the mapping stage in between; in that step write one parley.git.push event per update in command order through the event component, with the fields of the PRD (before null for a create, after null for a delete, created, deleted, forced, direct, via, session id or null, actor_type after the credential, the request's workspace slug), and delete the journal entry, all in one store transaction
- 8.6 When that transaction fails, log it, keep the journal entry and still return the request as accepted
- 8.7 Add RegisterPostPushListener and end the event step, whether or not its transaction succeeded, by calling every registered listener on its own goroutine with the slug, the accepted updates in command order, via and the session id (or none), recovering a panic and ignoring an error; do this for via git, api and land alike, so that package 21 and package 25 send no notification of their own, and call none for a refused request
- 8.8 Add Reconcile: for every journal entry, compare each ref with its after value (absent for a delete); when they agree write the entry's events and remove it in one transaction; when the refs still hold their before values remove the entry without events; running it on an empty journal does nothing
- 8.9 Register Reconcile in internal/hub/gitserver.go as a start hook of package 03, so that it completes before the listener accepts requests
- 8.10 Write no event for a refused push, a pack failure or a request with no commands
